findings.title: the documents have status --json say that the gateway's PID holds the socket, which status never checks
findings.cause: three statements read that the agents' client sends the key once status --json says the gateway runs at a loopback address whose listening socket its PID holds; status reads the record and whether its PID still runs llama-swap, and looks at no socket; only up checks the socket, through ports.listens, and the check of the socket is the client's own, from /proc
findings.consequence: a reader of the security document takes running: true for proof that the gateway holds the port; while up waits for a llama-swap it has recorded, status --json says running with a process that may not hold the port, so a client written from these lines, reading status --json alone, sends the key to whoever holds it
findings.fix: reword the three statements so that status --json gives whether the gateway runs, its address and its PID, and the client itself checks from /proc that this PID holds the listening socket; say in docs/commands.md, beside the fields a client relies on, that status does not look at the socket

findings.title: no test holds the newline that ends a --json document
findings.cause: every test of a --json output parses its stdout with serde_json, which reads a document the same with or without its last newline, so text.push('\n') in json_text can go with every test green
findings.consequence: with the push removed, status --json and doctor --json end without a newline, which only a shell's prompt, printed on the document's last line, shows
findings.fix: assert in status_json_without_a_gateway_exits_3_with_its_document that stdout ends with a closing brace and a newline
findings.test: status_json_without_a_gateway_exits_3_with_its_document, watched failing with the push removed
findings.evidence: read: src/presentation/mod.rs:149-153 and the three tests of status --json and doctor_exits_1_when_a_check_fails in tests/cli.rs, each going through serde_json::from_slice
